abstract: Industrially relevant cell lines include direct production hosts for biologics, vaccines, and viral vectors, as well as biomedical models that serve as references for host-cell engineering and comparative studies. However, their genomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiles, together with literature-derived phenotype information, remain distributed across different repositories, project outputs, and publications. Here, we present iCellOmics (https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/icellomics), an open-access database that integrates multi-omics data for industrially relevant cell lines within a unified data and analysis framework. The current release covers 17 cell lines and provides reference genomes for seven species, encompassing 144 018 protein-coding genes, 170 408 888 genomic variants, 673 differential-expression comparisons, 30 distinct single-cell RNA-seq BioProjects comprising 1 047 274 cells, 287 089 415 ATAC-seq peaks, 37 213 deduplicated literature-curated gene-phenotype relationships spanning 104 standardized phenotype subcategories. The database supports both cell line-centric browsing of available datasets and gene-centric exploration of cross-omics analysis results. Additionally, iCellOmics offers online GO and KEGG enrichment analysis tools to facilitate further data exploration. In summary, iCellOmics provides a valuable starting point for investigating gene-phenotype relationships in industrially relevant cell lines and supports cell-line engineering and the development of improved producer lines.
